name: codex
description: Codex integration: /codex second opinion and build delegation, Codex Companion background review and acceptance judge (its hooks are wired by the native hooks/hooks.json)

codex_companion._doc_codex_binary: Leave codex_binary unset to find codex on PATH; to point at a specific executable, set it in the codex_companion section of workflow/config.local.json (tools/codex-companion/judge_backend.resolve_codex_bin: a configured path that does not exist also falls back to PATH).
codex_companion._doc_assessment_timeout: Time limit in seconds for one codex call made by the background review subprocess (audit.py); the Stop hook does not wait for it, so it does not affect wrap-up time.
codex_companion._doc_codex_extra_args: Flags appended verbatim to codex exec (added by tools/codex-call.py; the acceptance judge goes through it too). Flags needed on one machine only (for example, disabling an MCP server registered in that machine's ~/.codex/config.toml that the judge does not need) go in the codex_companion section of workflow/config.local.json.

soft_gate._doc: completion_evidence = wrap-up self-check (heuristics): when silent_advisory=false and severity reaches block_severity_threshold, it only writes a completion_evidence assessment file and attaches a note to the next turn; it never blocks the wrap-up. handoff_review = ask Codex to review when a next-phase / handoff file is written (this key applies while the coding guard is off; while it is on, handoff_review_v6 applies, unset = off). With both off, handoffs rely on the self-review in skills/handoff Step 3.5; for a second opinion, call the codex skill.

fallback._doc: Fallback judge (tools/codex-companion/judge_backend.py): when codex is missing (neither the codex_binary path nor PATH finds it) or not authorized (not logged in / 401 / 429 / quota), headless `claude -p --model <model>` acts as the judge instead. Its independence is weaker (same vendor and model family, correlated blind spots), so it only issues advisories and never blocks the wrap-up (the acceptance judge only records, whichever backend it uses). Authorization failures write a suppression marker to workflow/companion-backend.json; codex is not retried within reprobe_hours, and the marker is cleared once codex succeeds. Empty claude_binary = find it automatically (PATH -> VS Code extension -> ~/.local/share/claude/versions). If neither is available, it falls back to heuristics only and says so once at SessionStart. Turn everything off with enabled:false.

audit_quota._doc: Quota buckets (INV-BUDGET-ISOLATION): within the shared max_audits_per_session total, acceptance_review has its own cap (max) and a reserved minimum (min; other reviews can use at most the total minus min), so neither kind starves the other.

acceptance_review._doc: Acceptance judge (hooks/codex_companion.py): governed by the coding-guard master switch; when that is off, neither trigger (claiming completion at wrap-up, marking a spec file done) runs. A completion claim bound to the session's single open spec -> builds a case file (the user's original request + acceptance checklist + diff samples + test output) and sends it to codex from a background subprocess (audit.py) for a verdict; Stop does not wait and never blocks. The result lands in a companion-assessment file, and the next UserPromptSubmit always attaches one line (verdict / severity / summary); the full explanation (summary + evidence + advice) is attached only on fail with severity at or above max_inject_severity. Every verdict is written to acceptance-audit.jsonl. Binding contract: review only when there is exactly one open spec, otherwise uncertain (INV-CASE-BINDING-OR-UNCERTAIN). max_per_spec = audits per spec per session. Turn off with enabled:false.
